answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. This is resilient because unearned rewards are capped and eventually burned, so an attacker cannot bank on a runaway Sybil campaign paying off. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a hollow as the anchor of the cost.
